q: In Spring AOP, what is a join point always?
explain: Proxies can only intercept method calls that go through them. AspectJ supports many more join point kinds.

q: Which advice type can prevent the target method from running at all?
explain: @Around decides whether to call `proceed()`. @Before can only stop the call by throwing an exception.

q: When does `@After` advice run?
options: After the method, whether it returned normally or threw (like finally)
Before the method returns its value
explain: @AfterReturning is for success only, @AfterThrowing for exceptions only.

q: Why is the transaction ignored here?
options: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy, so no transaction advice runs
explain: `save()` is called on `this`, the raw target, not on the proxy. Move it to another bean, or call it through the proxy.

q: Which proxy type does Spring Boot use by default?
explain: Boot sets `spring.aop.proxy-target-class=true`, so injecting by concrete class works even when the bean implements interfaces.

q: A bean implements `PaymentService` and is proxied with a JDK dynamic proxy. Another bean injects `StripePaymentService` (the class). What happens?
options: BeanNotOfRequiredTypeException: the proxy only implements the interface
The raw bean is injected without the proxy
explain: A JDK proxy is a `$Proxy` class implementing the interfaces, not a subclass. Inject the interface, or use class-based proxies.

q: A `@Transactional` method is declared `final` in a CGLIB-proxied bean. What happens when it's called from another bean?
options: It runs without a transaction: CGLIB can't override final methods
It runs in a transaction normally
explain: The subclass can't override it, so the call goes straight to the target, silently. Watch out in Kotlin, where classes and methods are final by default (the kotlin-spring plugin opens them).

q: What happens with `@Transactional` on a `private` method?
options: It works if called from the same class
explain: Private methods can't be overridden by a subclass proxy and are always called directly. Spring 6 does support protected and package-private methods on class-based proxies.

q: Which pointcut matches every method of every class in `com.shop.service` and its subpackages?
explain: `..` after the package means "this package and subpackages", `*.*` = any class, any method, and `(..)` = any arguments. `within(com.shop.service..*)` would also work.

q: How do you target all methods annotated with your own `@Audited` annotation?
explain: @annotation matches the method's annotation; @within matches the declaring class's annotation. The annotation needs RUNTIME retention.

q: What's wrong with this @Around advice?
options: It discards the method's return value: callers always get null
explain: Store and return the result: `Object result = pjp.proceed(); ... return result;`, and put the logging in a finally block to time failures too.

q: How does Spring AOP weave aspects?
options: At runtime, by wrapping beans in proxies
At compile time with the ajc compiler
explain: Spring can also use AspectJ load-time weaving (`@EnableLoadTimeWeaving`), but the default is proxies created by a BeanPostProcessor.

q: Which of these can AspectJ do that Spring AOP can't?
options: Intercept field access, constructors and self-invocations, on any object
explain: AspectJ changes the bytecode itself, so there's no proxy to bypass.

q: Two aspects apply to one method: @Order(1) LoggingAspect and @Order(2) SecurityAspect, both @Around. Which one is outermost?
options: LoggingAspect: a lower value means higher precedence
explain: Highest precedence runs first on the way in and last on the way out, like nested try blocks.

q: A method has both `@Retryable` and `@Transactional`. How should the advice be ordered?
options: Retry outside the transaction, so each attempt gets a fresh transaction
explain: If the transaction wraps the retry, all attempts share one transaction that's already marked rollback-only after the first failure.

q: An object is created with `new OrderService()` and its method has `@Cacheable`. Is the result cached?
options: No: only Spring-managed beans get proxies
explain: Annotations are just metadata; the proxy is what does the work. AspectJ weaving would be needed for objects outside the container.

q: Can `@AfterThrowing` advice swallow the exception?
options: No: the exception keeps propagating (the advice can throw a different one)
explain: To translate or suppress an exception, use @Around with try/catch around `proceed()`.

q: Which is a typical cross-cutting concern?
options: Mapping a DTO to an entity
explain: Cross-cutting = needed uniformly in many places, independent of the business logic: transactions, security, logging, metrics, caching.

q: Which component creates the AOP proxies for @Aspect classes in Spring?
explain: After a bean is initialized, it checks which advisors match the bean and wraps it in a proxy if any do.

q: What's the difference between `execution(...)` and `within(...)` pointcuts?
options: execution matches method signatures; within matches all methods of types in a given package or type
execution only works for public classes
explain: `within(com.shop.web..*)` = every method in the web layer; execution allows filtering by return type, name and parameters.

q: How does a Spring Data repository interface get an implementation?
options: Spring creates a proxy at runtime whose interceptors implement the query methods
You must write an Impl class
Hibernate generates it at build time
explain: The proxy routes CRUD methods to SimpleJpaRepository and derives queries from method names, with transaction and exception translation advice on top.

q: An `@Async` method is called from another method of the same bean. How does it run?
explain: Same self-invocation problem as @Transactional: no proxy, no executor hand-off.

q: What does the Spring-specific `bean(...)` pointcut designator match?
options: Beans by name, with wildcards, e.g. bean(*Service)
explain: It isn't part of AspectJ itself; it works only in Spring's proxy-based AOP.

q: In an advice method, what can a `JoinPoint` parameter give you?
options: The method signature, arguments and target object
explain: `getSignature()`, `getArgs()`, `getTarget()`, `getThis()` (the proxy). @Around gets the ProceedingJoinPoint subtype with `proceed()`.
